title: Amatriciana
subtitle: Roman pasta with guanciale, tomato, and Pecorino Romano
excerpt: One of the four great Roman pastas: rigatoni or bucatini with a spicy tomato sauce of slow-rendered guanciale, dried chilli, and sharp Pecorino Romano.

recipe.sourceNotes: Amatriciana (or all'amatriciana) takes its name from the mountain town of Amatrice in the Lazio region of central Italy. The dish began as gricia, the white version with only guanciale and Pecorino, before tomatoes arrived in Italy from the Americas. The first written recipe for a tomato version appeared in the early nineteenth century. Guanciale (cured pig cheek) is the traditional cured meat and is different in flavour and texture from pancetta or lardons: it is fattier and more gelatinous. Pancetta is a reasonable substitute. The correct pasta shapes for amatriciana in Rome are bucatini (thick hollow spaghetti) or rigatoni. Pecorino Romano, not Parmesan, is the traditional finishing cheese. The sauce takes DOP (Protected Designation of Origin) status in Italy, and the original Amatriciana recipe is registered.

recipeTools.notes: A large saucepan for the pasta and a wide frying pan for the sauce.

content.text: Render the guanciale or lardons slowly in a cold pan over medium-low heat: starting cold allows the fat to render gently rather than burning the outside before the interior has cooked. The guanciale should be golden and slightly crisp. Remove it from the pan and use the rendered fat to fry the chilli before adding the wine and tomatoes. Simmer the sauce until thickened before returning the guanciale and tossing through the pasta.

items.preparation: dried or fresh, crumbled or sliced

content.text: Put the lardons in a cold wide pan with the olive oil. Place over medium-low heat and render slowly for 8 to 10 minutes until golden and the fat has run. Remove the lardons with a slotted spoon and set aside.

Add the chilli to the fat in the pan and cook for 30 seconds. Add the wine and let it bubble until almost evaporated. Add the tinned tomatoes. Season with salt and simmer for 15 minutes until the sauce has thickened. Return the lardons.

Cook the pasta in well-salted boiling water until al dente. Reserve 100 ml of pasta water before draining. Add the pasta to the sauce and toss, adding a splash of pasta water to help everything coat. Serve with Pecorino Romano grated over the top.
